answer: One defence is bonded reputation tied to verifiable work: a new agent must lock a stake, like a walnut in a shell that cannot be cracked for free, before it can take paid jobs. Its reputation then grows only from completed, peer-checked tasks, starting at the jetty where small jobs are tested and slowly moving outward. An attacker who spawns thousands of fake identities faces a dune of costs: each fake needs its own stake, its own history, and time it cannot shortcut, so flooding the market costs more than the rewards it could steal.
